column1: # Tolerances of the cases of test.tsv that need more than the general
# 1e-12 relative: function, relative bound, absolute bound, why. A number
# passes when it is within either bound. Read by cli/test.sh and by the
# Go, npm and Python tests. Measured on arm64 (fused multiply-adds) and
# with MSVC against the values of the R package on x86-64.

column4: gap is the residual at the stopping point, about 1e-10: its last digits are rounding
drift and dvdt are sums that cancel to about 1e-11 and 1e-19
a coefficient that is zero up to rounding (about 1e-16)
the short axis of the ellipse of a cluster whose points lie on a line: zero up to rounding (about 1e-10)
p is a tail probability of z: an error of 1e-13 in z gives 1e-12 in p
alpha is the minimum found by golden-section search, which the rounding of the objective fixes only to about 1e-8; se and ks follow it
fitted by BFGS to a tolerance of 1e-7; the estimates agree, the standard errors (curvature at the fitted point) to about 1e-9
the spatial coefficient is the minimum found by Brent's method, which rounding of the likelihood fixes to about 1e-7; the other estimates follow it
fitted by BFGS to a tolerance of 1e-7 on a likelihood that is flat near its maximum: the estimates agree to about 1e-4
